children: OneKey founder Yishi urged users to move seed phrases stored on iPhone 11 and earlier models, saying iOS updates cannot fix the devices’ chip-level vulnerabilities. According to PANews, Yishi said on November 1 that erasing an older iPhone, enabling airplane mode and using it only to store a seed phrase may not be as safe as many people assume.

The affected models include the iPhone XS, XR and 11 series, as well as the second-generation iPhone SE. They have BootROM hardware vulnerabilities, including checkm8 and usbliter8, that cannot be fixed through software updates. An attacker with physical access could connect a specially designed USB device through DFU mode and execute code before the operating system starts.

title: OneKey Founder Urges iPhone 11 and Earlier Users to Migrate Seed Phrases
